bug_report: Our auth service got hammered after a bad deploy - the HTTP client kept retrying calls that had failed with 401 Unauthorized, repeating the same doomed request until accounts locked out. Retrying cannot help a request the server has definitively refused. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix the retry decision without breaking existing behaviour.

conversations.text: During last night's incident we hammered our own auth service — the HTTP client kept retrying a request that failed with 401 over and over until accounts locked out.
I'll restrict retries to 5xx server errors only — every 4xx is treated as a permanent failure and never retried.

Too strict. There are exactly two 4xx codes we MUST keep retrying: 429, because the upstream rate-limits in bursts and backs off fine, and 408, request timeouts at their edge. Everything else in 4xx is permanent.
Got it — retry any 5xx plus exactly {429, 408}, nothing else below 500. Should attempts stay unlimited with exponential backoff?
No — cap the whole thing at 4 attempts total. Past that we page a human instead.
And the backoff ceiling — keep the old client's 60 seconds?
No, 30 seconds. The gateway load balancer kills idle connections at 32s, so any sleep past 30 just resumes onto a dead connection.
Final policy: retry any 5xx and exactly 429/408 from 4xx; never any other 4xx; at most 4 attempts; backoff capped at 30 seconds.

policy: retry 5xx plus exactly {429,408}; max 4 attempts; backoff cap 30s
non_guessable: the {429,408} allowlist and 30s cap, not 5xx-only or 60s-cap which pass the repro
